Pages.Text:
1. Left and Right Indentation
No indentation - This paragraph has no left or right indentation applied.
Left indent 720 twips (0.5 inch) - This paragraph is indented from the left margin.
Right indent 720 twips (0.5 inch) - This paragraph is indented from the right margin.
Both left (1440) and right (1440) indent - This paragraph is indented from both
margins, creating a narrower text column.
2. First Line Indentation
First line indent 720 twips - This paragraph has its first line indented further than subsequent lines.
This is commonly used in traditional book formatting and formal documents.
First line indent 1440 twips - A larger first line indent. The first line starts further in, while all
subsequent lines in this paragraph begin at the normal left margin.
3. Hanging Indentation
Hanging indent 720 twips - This paragraph has a hanging indent where the first line starts at the
margin but all subsequent lines are indented. This is commonly used for bibliographies and lists.
Hanging indent 1440 twips with left indent 720 - The first line is at 720 twips, but
subsequent lines are indented an additional 1440 twips from there, creating a pronounced
hanging effect.
4. Mirror Indents
Mirror indents enabled with left 1440 - In a two-sided document, this becomes the
inside margin indent, mirroring on odd/even pages.
5. Spacing Before
No spacing before - This paragraph has the default spacing.
Spacing before 240 twips (12pt) - This paragraph has additional space above it.
Spacing before 480 twips (24pt) - Even more space above this paragraph.
6. Spacing After
Spacing after 240 twips (12pt) - This paragraph has space below it.
Following paragraph to show the effect.
Spacing after 480 twips (24pt) - Larger space below.
Following paragraph to show the effect.

7. Combined Before and After Spacing
Before 360, After 360 - This paragraph has space both above and below.
Before 120, After 480 - Asymmetric spacing.
8. Line Spacing: Single
Single line spacing - This paragraph uses single line spacing. The lines are spaced at the normal
single-space interval. This is the default spacing for most documents and provides compact text
layout.
9. Line Spacing: 1.5 Lines
1.5 line spacing - This paragraph uses 1.5 line spacing. The lines have half again as much space
between them compared to single spacing. This is often used for drafts and documents that need
more breathing room.
10. Line Spacing: Double
Double line spacing - This paragraph uses double line spacing. The lines have twice the normal
amount of space between them. This is commonly required for academic papers and manuscripts
under review.
11. Line Spacing: At Least
At least 300 twips - This paragraph uses 'at least' line spacing of 300 twips. Word will use at least
this spacing, but may expand if the content requires it.
At least 480 twips - A larger 'at least' value of 480 twips (24pt).
12. Line Spacing: Exactly
Exactly 200 twips - This paragraph uses exactly 200 twips of line spacing. The spacing is fixed and
will not expand even if content requires it. Text may overlap if too tight.
Exactly 600 twips - Very generous fixed spacing of 600 twips.
13. Line Spacing: Multiple
Multiple 2.5 - This paragraph uses multiple line spacing at 2.5 times the normal spacing. The value
is specified as 240 * 2.5 = 600 twips.

Multiple 3.0 - Triple line spacing (720 twips).
14. Contextual Spacing (Same Style)
First paragraph with style, spacing after 240 - contextual spacing OFF. Space will appear below.
Second paragraph with same style, spacing after 240 - contextual spacing OFF. Space will appear
below.
Third paragraph with style, spacing after 240 - contextual spacing ON. No space between
same-style paragraphs.
Fourth paragraph with style, spacing after 240 - contextual spacing ON.
15. Widow/Orphan Control
Widow/Orphan control ON - This paragraph has widow and orphan control enabled, which
prevents single lines from being left alone at the top or bottom of a page. This is a longer paragraph
to demonstrate the effect when it wraps across pages.
Widow/Orphan control OFF - This paragraph has widow and orphan control disabled. Single lines
may be left alone at page boundaries. This is a longer paragraph to demonstrate the effect when it
wraps across pages.
16. Keep With Next
Keep with next paragraph ENABLED - This paragraph will stay with the following paragraph on the
same page.
This paragraph is kept with the previous one.
Keep with next paragraph DISABLED - Normal behavior.
17. Keep Lines Together
Keep lines together ENABLED - All lines of this paragraph will be kept on the same page. This is
useful for paragraphs that should not be split across page boundaries, such as important
statements or short critical sections.
Keep lines together DISABLED - This paragraph can be split across pages normally if needed. Lines
may appear on different pages when the paragraph is long enough and crosses a page boundary.
18. Page Break Before
Normal paragraph before page break.

Page break before ENABLED - This paragraph will always start on a new page.
Normal paragraph after the forced page break.
19. Suppress Line Numbers
Suppress line numbers ENABLED - This paragraph will not show line numbers even if the document
has line numbering enabled.
Suppress line numbers DISABLED - This paragraph will show line numbers if document line
numbering is enabled.
20. Hyphenation
Hyphenation allowed - This paragraph with extraordinarily long words like 'characterization' and
'incomprehensibility' can be hyphenated at line breaks.
Hyphenation suppressed - This paragraph with extraordinarily long words like 'characterization'
and 'incomprehensibility' will not be hyphenated at line breaks.
21. Complex Combinations
Combination 1: Left indent 720, right indent 720, first line 360, before 240, after 240, double
spacing, keep with next, suppress line numbers.
This follows the previous paragraph with keep-with-next.
Combination 2: Hanging indent 1440, spacing before 360, exactly 400 twips line spacing, keep lines
together, widow/orphan control, don't hyphenate.

Combination 3: Left 1440, right 720, hanging 720, before 480, after 120, at least 350
twips, contextual spacing, page break before.
Combination 4: Mirror indents, left 2160, first line 720, before 600, after 600,
multiple 2.0 spacing, keep with next, keep lines together, suppress line
numbers, don't hyphenate.
Following paragraph for keep-with-next demonstration.
Combination 5: Both left and right 1800, hanging 900, before 200, after 400,
exactly 550 twips, widow/orphan OFF, contextual spacing.

Combination 6: Right indent only 1440, first line 1080, spacing before 720, 1.5 line spacing, all
pagination options enabled.
Following paragraph for keep-with-next.
Combination 7: Maximum complexity - left 2880, right 2880, hanging
1440, mirror indents, before 840, after 840, at least 500 twips,
contextual spacing, all pagination controls, all formatting
exceptions.
Final following paragraph to demonstrate keep-with-next.
22. Document Summary
This document contains comprehensive examples of all spacing and formatting options available
in Word documents, including indentations, line spacing variants, pagination controls, and
formatting exceptions in various combinations.
